plan: 'View and plan of Sinderdroo or Melundy, on the Malabar coast' (survey by Co. John Watson, 1765; engraved P. Begbie; publ. A. Dalrymple, 25 July 1774; BnF Gallica btv1b532583381 via Wikimedia Commons, public domain; catalogue SIN-02)
pixel_frame: 2x enlargement of the native crop (1450,3850)-(2350,4400) of the 4110x5340 scan; x right, y down. The fort is about 530 native pixels across: this is a hydrographic chart, not a fort plan.
method: similarity transform from the traced wall outline (39 vertices read by eye, checked by overlay) to the OSM islet coastline (way 19804981, 291 vertices; local metres, x east, y north). Fitted by maximising polygon overlap (IoU) over scale 0.35-1.30, rotation 0-360 deg, shift +-60 m, then refined. The only free choice was the outline; no interior feature was used.

fit.result: one clear peak: IoU 0.91 at 269 deg; the best orientation more than 30 deg away scores 0.56 (at 90 deg, the 180-degree flip of an elongated shape). The chart is rotated about 90 deg from north-up

validation_not_in_fit.result: 1 nautical mile = about 1261 native px = 1.47 m/px against 1.36 m/px fitted (8% difference)
traced outline 19.0 ha; OSM island 19.2 ha; written sources 48 acres (19.4 ha)

validation_not_in_fit.offset_m: A1 12, A2 32, B3 33, B4 33, S1 72, S2 61 (nearest mapped building): only A1 is corroborated

not_traced: about 30 small blocks and houses and the trees drawn inside; bastion bumps on the wall (too ambiguous to count); the sea approaches, soundings and Rajacoote/Pudendroo; any gate
traced_by: visual reading of crops; pixel coordinates are in tools/trace/curation/sindhudurg.mjs
